stories.headline: China's CXMT posts $21B first-half revenue and blows past its own profit guidance by 36%

key_facts.fact: CXMT reported first-half 2026 revenue of 150.31 billion yuan, up 873.6% year on year
key_facts.excerpt: CXMT reported 1H26 revenue of RMB 150.31bn, up 873% YoY.

key_facts.fact: Net profit attributable to shareholders reached 77.61 billion yuan, versus a 2.33 billion yuan loss in the first half of 2025
key_facts.excerpt: 1H net profit attributable to shareholders was RMB 77.61bn, versus a RMB 2.33bn loss a year earlier. Excluding non-recurring items, attributable net profit was RMB 78.79bn.

key_facts.fact: The result came in about 36% above the top end of the company's July guidance of 50-57 billion yuan in attributable net profit
key_facts.excerpt: The results significantly exceeded the company's July guidance for 1H attributable net profit of RMB 50-57bn. The actual figure of RMB 77.61bn was approximately 36% above the upper end of guidance.

key_facts.fact: First-half revenue compares with 15.44 billion yuan a year earlier, close to a tenfold increase, implying a net margin of roughly 52%
key_facts.excerpt: 1H revenue surged to 150.3B yuan vs. 15.44B yuan a year ago — almost 10x growth year-over-year; 1H net income hit 77.6B yuan, implying a massive ~52% profit margin

key_facts.fact: It is CXMT's first earnings report since its July STAR Market listing; the stock is up more than 570% since debut and the company briefly became China's most valuable listed firm at 3.3 trillion yuan
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of China's homegrown memory chipmaker have jumped more than 570% since listing... That guidance helped fuel the stock's blockbuster debut late July, when CXMT reached a market value of 3.3 trillion yuan.

key_facts.fact: CXMT trades at about 10 times estimated 2027 earnings, which Goldman Sachs calls a significant discount to global peers
key_facts.excerpt: CXMT trades at about 10 times estimated 2027 earnings, a 'significant discount to global peers', according to Goldman Sachs.

stories.headline: Nvidia pauses its revenue-sharing deals with AI cloud providers after internal antitrust worries

key_facts.fact: Nvidia paused some deals in the financing program that gave credit support to AI cloud companies in exchange for a share of their revenue, stepping back from it last week
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia has paused some deals that were part of its new financing initiative that offered credit support to AI cloud companies in exchange for a share of revenue... stepped back from the program last week, the Journal said, adding that it could still revamp the initiative later or fold it into another program.

key_facts.fact: Under the proposed structure Nvidia would take 50% of any revenue a cloud provider earned from its chips above an agreed threshold, and would rent back capacity the provider could not sell
key_facts.excerpt: Under the proposed deals, Nvidia would receive 50 per cent of any revenue cloud providers earned through its chips beyond a certain threshold... Nvidia had sought to rent compute capacity back from cloud customers if they were unable to sell it.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia disclosed the program's size for the first time this week: $36 billion in commitments under agreements that typically run six years, with CFO Colette Kress saying it could generate billions over the medium to long term
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia disclosed the scale of the programme for the first time this week, revealing $36 billion in commitments under agreements typically running six years... CFO Colette Kress told investors the arrangement could generate billions of dollars for Nvidia over the medium to long term.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia employees raised concerns internally and with customers that the program could draw antitrust scrutiny; providers objected to being told they could rent the chips only to approved customers
key_facts.excerpt: some Nvidia employees expressed concerns to current and potential customers that the initiative could draw antitrust scrutiny... Nvidia told some cloud providers they could only rent its chips out to approved customers.

key_facts.fact: Sharon AI and Firmus Technologies were named as the first participants when the program launched in July
key_facts.excerpt: Sharon AI and Firmus Technologies were named as the first participants when the programme launched in July.

key_facts.fact: The pause follows Nvidia helping arrange $500 billion in financing for customers this month and guaranteeing up to $105 billion for an OpenAI data-center lease; Nvidia says the July business model remains in place
key_facts.excerpt: The company in August helped arrange US$500 billion in financing from major US financial institutions for its customers, and also agreed to guarantee up to US$105 billion to help OpenAI lease a massive data centre.

stories.headline: Anthropic weighed buying AI chip startup MatX for about $7B, then dropped the deal

key_facts.fact: Anthropic discussed buying AI chip startup MatX for roughly $7 billion to speed up its custom hardware effort, according to two people briefed on the matter
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic discussed buying artificial intelligence chip startup MatX for roughly $7 billion, seeking to accelerate efforts to develop custom hardware for its fast-growing AI business, two people briefed on the matter told Reuters.

key_facts.fact: The merger talks are no longer active and have evolved into a discussion about a partnership; Reuters could not learn why they stopped
key_facts.excerpt: The merger talks, which a third person said have evolved into a discussion about a partnership... Reuters is reporting on the discussions for the first time but could not learn why the talks are no longer active.

key_facts.fact: MatX, founded by former Google TPU engineers, is now seeking new capital at a valuation of about $4 billion — roughly half the price discussed in the abandoned deal
key_facts.excerpt: MatX, founded by former Google tensor processing unit (TPU) engineers, is now seeking to raise new capital at a valuation of about $4 billion, one of the people said.

key_facts.fact: MatX has been working on a chip aimed at training large AI models; buying it would have given Anthropic in-house design expertise and lower long-term costs
key_facts.excerpt: An acquisition of an AI chip startup such as MatX would give Anthropic in-house design expertise and could help lower costs over the longer term... MatX has been working on a chip that would be useful for building large AI models in a process called training.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is hiring chip experts and exploring multiple designs to cut its reliance on Nvidia while it prepares an IPO
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic aims to accelerate in-house chip design to reduce reliance on Nvidia and support its AI models... The company is hiring chip experts and exploring multiple chip designs, balancing purchases from Nvidia, Google, and cloud providers.

stories.headline: XPeng raises over $900M for its robotics arm at a $6.3B valuation, a record for China's embodied AI

key_facts.fact: XPeng's robotics business signed share purchase agreements raising over $900 million at a post-money valuation above $6.3 billion, announced on 27 August 2026
key_facts.excerpt: XPENG robotics business raises over US$900 million, at a post-money valuation of over US$6.3 billion, marking the largest single-round private financing ever recorded in China's embodied AI industry... Milan, 27 August 2026

key_facts.fact: The round was led by IDG Capital with Gaorong Ventures participating and Tencent and Alibaba as strategic investors
key_facts.excerpt: This round was initiated by leading global investors, led by IDG Capital, with participation from Gaorong Ventures and support from Tencent and Alibaba as strategic investors.

key_facts.fact: The company says it is the largest single-round private capital raise in China's embodied AI industry to date; the robotics unit stays consolidated in XPeng's financial statements
key_facts.excerpt: which marks the largest single-round private capital raise in China's embodied AI industry to date... Upon closing, [the robotics business will] continue to be consolidated [in the] Group's financial statements.

key_facts.fact: Its IRON humanoid is due to enter mass production by the end of 2026, first deployed in XPeng stores and campuses, with deliveries in China and overseas in 2027
key_facts.excerpt: XPENG IRON is expected to enter mass production by the end of 2026, with initial commercial deployment at XPENG's stores and campuses, before officially launching and beginning deliveries in China and overseas markets in 2027.

key_facts.fact: IRON has 76 degrees of freedom in its body and 21 in each hand, and runs on three of XPeng's in-house Turing AI chips delivering up to 2,250 trillion operations per second
key_facts.excerpt: It boasts 76 degrees of freedom in its body and 21 in each hand for human-like dexterity. Powered by three of the company's Turing AI chips, IRON achieves up to 2,250 trillion operations per second.

stories.headline: Georgia regulators approve Georgia Power's 3,200 MW contract to feed OpenAI's Effingham data center

key_facts.fact: Georgia Power announced on 27 August that the Georgia Public Service Commission approved its contract to serve OpenAI's new project in Effingham County
key_facts.excerpt: Today, Georgia Power announced that its contract to serve OpenAI's new project in Effingham County has been approved as part of the regulatory process with the Georgia Public Service Commission (PSC).

key_facts.fact: The contract, filed with the PSC in July, covers 3,200 megawatts of new demand and includes up to 1,000 MW of flexible demand response Georgia Power can curtail at peak
key_facts.excerpt: The company's contract with OpenAI was filed with the Georgia PSC in July and includes 3,200 megawatts (MW) of new demand. Under that agreement, OpenAI will pay the full cost of the infrastructure needed to serve it and has committed up to 1,000 MW of flexible demand response.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI pays the full cost of the infrastructure needed to serve the site
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI will pay the full cost of the infrastructure needed to serve it

key_facts.fact: Georgia Power says its portfolio of large-load contracts will bring roughly $950 million a year in incremental revenue, worth $2.847 billion to customers over 2029-2031
key_facts.excerpt: projected incremental revenue from new large-load customers that is expected to provide savings of approximately $950 million per year, increasing customer benefits to $2.847 billion over the three-year period of 2029-2031.

key_facts.fact: A typical residential customer using 1,000 kWh a month is now expected to save at least $15 a month from 2029, up from the company's December 2025 commitment of $102 a year
key_facts.excerpt: Georgia Power customers are expected to see savings of at least $15 per month beginning in 2029 for the typical residential customer using 1,000 kilowatt-hours per month, an increase from the company's December 2025 commitment of $102 per year to $180 per year.

sources.title: Georgia Power's contract with OpenAI approved; Latest approval part of portfolio of large-load contracts delivering approximately $950 million in annual savings beginning in 2029

stories.headline: Nvidia files to create NVPAC, its first employee-funded political action committee

key_facts.fact: Nvidia filed a statement of organization on Thursday for a political action committee formally named the Nvidia Corporation Employees Federal Political Action Committee
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia filed a statement of organization Thursday, with the PAC's official name being the Nvidia Corporation Employees Federal Political Action Committee.

key_facts.fact: The committee, known as NVPAC, will be funded by eligible employees who can each contribute up to $5,000; Bloomberg Government first reported its creation
key_facts.excerpt: The super PAC, first reported by Bloomberg Government, will be funded by eligible employees who can give up to $5,000.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia is stepping up efforts to influence US policy and joins Meta and Alphabet's Google in running a committee to spend on elections
key_facts.excerpt: Tech company Nvidia will start an employee-funded political action committee, a source familiar with the plans told Reuters, as the company seeks to step up its efforts to influence U.S. policy. The group will be called NVPAC... Nvidia joins other tech giants, including Meta Platforms and Alphabet's Google.

key_facts.fact: FEC records show Nvidia executives Gavin Sherry and Sundeep Madra gave $443,000 to the Republican National Committee on 24 June
key_facts.excerpt: Records from the Federal Election Commission indicate executives Gavin Sherry and Sundeep Madra gave $443,000 to the Republican National Committee on June 24.

key_facts.fact: The move follows a year in which CEO Jensen Huang repeatedly met administration officials and lawmakers as Washington debates AI regulation and chip export rules
key_facts.excerpt: It is the latest move in Washington for Nvidia and its CEO Jensen Huang, who developed a strong relationship with President Trump at the start of his second term. Huang has met with administration officials and lawmakers on Capitol Hill numerous times this year.
